scenario: Two paediatric surgery teams, Team Cobalt and Team Indigo, are measured on complication-free surgery rates. Team Cobalt handles predominantly complex multi-organ procedures; Team Indigo mostly performs straightforward single-organ operations.

data.description: complication-free surgery rates by procedure complexity and entity

question: (a) Which entity has the higher aggregate complication-free surgery rate? (b) Which entity performs better within each procedure complexity stratum? (c) Compute each entity's corrected rate using a 50/50 procedure complexity mix. (d) Which entity should be preferred, and why does the aggregate ranking mislead?

ground_truth.explanation: Team Indigo's higher aggregate is driven by its disproportionate assignment to easier straightforward single-organ cases. Team Cobalt outperforms Team Indigo in both procedure complexity strata. Standardising to a 50/50 procedure complexity mix gives Team Cobalt 0.895 vs Team Indigo 0.855; Team Cobalt is the superior performer once procedure complexity is controlled.

naive_answer: Team Indigo is better because its aggregate complication-free surgery rate (0.92) exceeds Team Cobalt's (0.8453).
naive_trap: Procedure complexity is a confounder: Team Cobalt handles the majority of harder complex multi-organ cases, depressing its aggregate while Team Indigo benefits from easier cases.
reasoning_trace: (1) Complex multi-organ: Team Cobalt 0.83 > Team Indigo 0.77. (2) Straightforward single-organ: Team Cobalt 0.96 > Team Indigo 0.94. (3) Team Cobalt handles 88.2% complex multi-organ cases vs Team Indigo's 11.8% — this pulls Team Cobalt's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: Team Cobalt=0.5×0.83+0.5×0.96=0.895; Team Indigo=0.5×0.77+0.5×0.94=0.855. Team Cobalt wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nA1,rA1,nA2,rA2 = 750,0.83,100,0.96
nB1,rB1,nB2,rB2 = 100,0.77,750,0.94
ovA=(nA1*rA1+nA2*rA2)/(nA1+nA2); ovB=(nB1*rB1+nB2*rB2)/(nB1+nB2)
assert ovB > ovA, 'naive: Team Indigo aggregate higher'
cA=0.5*rA1+0.5*rA2; cB=0.5*rB1+0.5*rB2
assert abs(cA-0.895)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.855)<0.005
assert cA > cB, 'corrected: Team Cobalt wins'
